identity.name: Sovereign Debt Repression & Real-Value Dilution
identity.stable_question: When sovereign debt-service and refinancing pressure rises, are fiscal, monetary, regulatory and balance-sheet policies shifting from market-clearing adjustment toward mechanisms that suppress the real cost of government funding or transfer duration/inflation risk to creditors; and is that shift economically material enough to change the cross-asset regime?

scope_routing.scope_boundary: Profile diagnoses sovereign funding, repression and real-value dilution mechanics. It does not create a new Credit World, does not assign a legal default status and does not authorize a trade.

theory_causal_mechanism.causal_mechanism: Rising sovereign debt-service and refinancing pressure can raise issuance burden and marginal funding costs. If market-clearing adjustment becomes politically or financially costly, authorities may respond through fiscal adjustment, debt-management changes, liquidity backstops, central-bank duration absorption, yield caps, regulatory captive demand or greater inflation tolerance. Financial repression exists only when policy persistently channels savings toward sovereign funding or suppresses the government's real funding cost relative to a defensible counterfactual. Real-value dilution exists only when creditors experience material purchasing-power erosion through negative real returns, inflation surprise or an equivalent policy-induced transfer. These mechanisms can form a reflexive loop in which higher yields raise interest expense and issuance needs, which further raise term premium and yields, increasing pressure for policy intervention.
assumptions: sovereign debt, maturity, fiscal and policy data are available with dated vintages
market-function interventions can be distinguished from persistent funding-cost suppression
real-return measures use declared inflation and horizon semantics
foreign-holder flows are treated as transmission variables rather than sufficient causal proof
reserve-currency status and capital controls are explicit routing variables
theory_causal_mechanism.claim_boundary: High debt, central-bank purchases, negative real yields, foreign selling, gold appreciation or Treasury buybacks are individually insufficient to prove financial repression or real-value dilution. SDR0 does not label an explicit legal default and prohibits unqualified 'soft_default' as a canonical state.
theory_causal_mechanism.theory_gap: Primary theory lineage is seeded but not automatically admitted as Canon TheoryObjects. Identification of fiscal dominance and repression remains episode-specific and must survive Gold Replay and hard negatives.

evidence.evidence_policy: Use point-in-time primary policy documents and official fiscal, debt-management, market-operation, auction, holdings, inflation and real-yield data. Academic and central-bank research may support mechanism claims. Secondary commentary may seed event locators or competing explanations but cannot establish the live state.
source_requirements: official fiscal or budget source for debt, deficit and interest-cost facts
official debt-management or auction source for issuance and market-function facts
central-bank primary source for purchase, repo, yield-target and policy-reaction claims
official cross-border holdings source for foreign-holder facts
official or institutionally governed data for inflation, real yields and expectations
separate evidence for regulatory captive-demand claims
independent mechanism evidence before causal labels are promoted

economic_definitions.fiscal_constraint: pressure created by primary balance, debt stock, interest burden and refinancing needs relative to fiscal capacity
economic_definitions.debt_service_pressure: interest and principal refinancing burden over the declared horizon, not debt stock alone
economic_definitions.financial_repression: persistent official policy that directs savings toward sovereign funding or suppresses sovereign borrowing costs relative to a defensible market-clearing counterfactual
economic_definitions.real_value_dilution: material creditor purchasing-power loss through negative real returns, inflation surprise or equivalent policy-induced transfer
economic_definitions.liquidity_backstop: temporary or standing facility designed primarily to prevent forced sales or restore market functioning
economic_definitions.captive_demand: regulatory, institutional or policy-induced demand that materially weakens normal price sensitivity for sovereign debt

input.revision_semantics: preserve first release, revised vintage and policy-event timestamp separately
input.missingness_policy: material missing fiscal, maturity, policy-objective or real-return evidence degrades the affected dimension to unknown; no silent imputation of repression state

identification_assumptions: policy response may be endogenous to the same fiscal or macro shock
central-bank asset purchases require objective and maturity-mix identification before repression labels
foreign-holder changes are not causal proof without hedge-adjusted alternatives
negative real yields are not sufficient evidence of financial repression
counterfactual market-clearing yields are uncertain and must be represented as ranges or competing models
event-study timing is not structural causal proof
inference.state_transition_logic: Track fiscal pressure, market-clearing stress, marginal demand, policy support, captive demand, real-rate suppression and creditor real loss as separate typed dimensions. A summary regime stage may be emitted only from declared AND gates; no majority vote or weighted master score.
inference.uncertainty_representation: vintage uncertainty, policy-objective ambiguity, counterfactual-yield range, identification status, competing mechanisms, horizon-specific confidence and unresolved-node flags

output.uncertainty_semantics: state authority is dimension-specific; summary stage cannot exceed the weakest binding evidence/identification requirement
output.confidence_semantics: high confidence requires primary policy/fiscal evidence, explicit objective classification, real-return evidence and bounded competing mechanisms

falsification_rules: debt_service burden stabilizes or falls through fiscal adjustment, growth or maturity management without repression
auction and marginal-demand conditions remain healthy despite higher issuance
long real yields remain positive and market-clearing while central-bank support is absent or clearly temporary
policy interventions prove time-limited market-function operations and exit without persistent suppression
no material new captive-demand mechanism appears
inflation expectations remain anchored and creditor real returns are not persistently negative
foreign-holder reductions are absorbed without material term-premium or funding stress
the candidate fiscal-dominance episode is better explained by a standard cyclical monetary-policy shock
revision_triggers: material regulatory change affecting sovereign demand
historical data revision that changes a Gold Replay classification
falsification_failure.degrade_behavior: downgrade only affected dimensions, preserve contradictory evidence, and force summary regime_stage to indeterminate when a binding gate is unresolved

benchmark_qualification.point_in_time_split_policy: freeze fiscal vintages, policy documents, market data and event knowledge exactly as available at each replay cut
benchmark_qualification.oos_policy: walk-forward episode replay and jurisdiction holdout where comparable data exist
benchmark_qualification.regime_holdout: at least one hard negative and one policy-exit episode must remain outside initial mechanism tuning
benchmark_qualification.false_alarm_accounting: count repression or real-value-dilution flags that later settle as temporary liquidity support, cyclical easing or ordinary market clearing
benchmark_qualification.calibration_requirement: required only if probabilistic transition outputs are introduced later
benchmark_qualification.multiple_testing_policy: pre-register primary state dimensions and event windows; penalize post-hoc threshold mining
benchmark_qualification.complexity_penalty: profile must improve state-transition discipline or false-positive control beyond debt, real-yield and balance-sheet-growth baselines

settlement_learning.settlement_rule: settle fiscal constraint, policy support, repression and real-value dilution as separate mechanism claims with supported, partially_supported, falsified or indeterminate outcomes; do not infer mechanism correctness from asset P&L alone
settlement_learning.replay_policy: preserve original policy text, fiscal data vintage, market data and knowledge cutoff; no future-policy backfill into earlier states
settlement_learning.revision_rule: revise profile semantics only after repeated Replay/Shadow evidence shows a state dimension or gate is unstable; breaking changes require a new contract version
